output.body: Take sum_to(n), which equals 1+2+...+n. Its smaller self is sum_to(n-1), so sum_to(n) equals n + sum_to(n-1). That chain of smaller problems has to end somewhere, and sum_to(0)=0 is where it ends.
output.key_idea: A recursive function solves a problem by handing a smaller version of the same problem to itself, and it stops at a base case that needs no further help.
output.question: Using that rule, what smaller sum_to call would sum_to(3) hand off to, and what would it add to that call's result?
